candidates.title: 4 Canadians aboard missing Ontario-based air ambulance flying from Bermuda
candidates.description: The U.S. Coast Guard is searching for an Ontario-based air ambulance jet that has gone missing with six people on board, including four Canadians, on Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman, 2 children dead after serious collision near Foam Lake, Sask.
candidates.description: A serious car crash left three people dead and four others injured. A 40-year old man from South Carolina was arrested and charged.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 3 Cape Bretoners were hit and killed by a train in Maine in 1970. Some want the case reopened
candidates.description: Kenny Novak, 15, David Burrows, 17, and Terry Burt, 20, were in sleeping bags on a rail track west of the border town of Houlton, Maine, when they were struck early on the morning of July 10, 1970, by a train. The deaths were ruled accidental, but questions persist about the deaths.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. lawyer found to have misappropriated $117K from dementia-stricken client
candidates.description: Leonard Hil Marriott also prepared documents to give himself 50 per cent ownership of the woman's condo and 75 per cent of her estate.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Internal documents detail Ottawa's economic worries over Alberta referendum
candidates.description: Internal federal documents offer insights into how Ottawa is assessing the economic fallout from the possibility of Alberta separating from Canada and becoming an independent state.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada bet billions on an EV boom. Was it too much, too soon?
candidates.description: The federal and provincial governments bet billions on the rapid rise of the electric vehicle industry. But major EV and battery projects in Ontario, Quebec and British Columbia have since been delayed, cancelled, suspended, substantially changed — and in one case, gone bankrupt — as automakers and suppliers adjust to weaker-than-anticipated demand.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Actor and advocate Michael J. Fox promoted to companion level in Order of Canada
candidates.description: Celebrated actor and Parkinson's disease activist Michael J. Fox said he felt both "pride" and "humility" while receiving a promotion within the Order of Canada on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What does Elections Alberta's compliance agreement with Forever Canadian mean?
candidates.description: A compliance agreement between Elections Alberta and a group campaigning for Alberta to remain in Canada means the organization is required to disclose certain referendum advertising expenses and contributions.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stellantis says tariffs, consumer demand driving weeks-long layoffs at Windsor plant
candidates.description: Global carmaker Stellantis says tariffs and consumer demand in North America are driving weeks-long layoffs at the company's plant in Windsor, Ont.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge in fatal N.L. case questions whether impaired driving sentences are working
candidates.description: A St. John's judge is questioning whether or not punishments are fitting the crime when it comes to impaired driving. Judge Bruce Short sentenced a man to five years in prison on Friday for a fatal crash in 2023.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 12 Jewish teachers file human rights complaints against group of Ontario school boards, unions
candidates.description: Twelve Jewish teachers have filed human rights complaints against a group of Ontario school boards and teachers' unions, alleging they have experienced discrimination at their workplaces due to incidents of antisemitism.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: No Canadians elected to world hockey governing body; Turkey, New Zealand represented
candidates.description: Hockey Canada president and chief executive officer Katherine Henderson was up for one of the minimum three female spots on the IIHF council at Friday's election, but was eliminated in the second of three rounds of voting in Tenerife, Spain. That means no Canadians have been elected to the council, a surprising result for a nation considered one of the sport's powerhouses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Legal battles mount over the off-reserve Millennium Scoop
candidates.description: Courts countrywide are grappling with the complex question of whether federal and provincial governments can be sued for the stark overrepresentation of Indigenous children in the off-reserve child welfare system, delivering dizzyingly mixed results.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stephen Harper warns Alberta separatism will bring 'no benefit'
candidates.description: Former Conservative prime minister Stephen Harper cautioned against the prospect of Alberta separation in a column Friday, writing that even voting just to "send a message" would represent a fraught approach.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A transgender musician was denied washroom access. P.E.I.'s music scene is taking a stand
candidates.description: Prince Edward Island's music scene is pushing back after a Charlottetown venue denied washroom access to a transgender musician.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Government inspection at 3 Ontario career colleges reported 'serious concerns,' court records show
candidates.description: Ontario government officials who inspected three Academy of Learning career colleges found evidence suggesting third parties were completing the coursework and a few students who couldn't name their school or program, they alleged in reports filed in court.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: It's the biggest Alberta separatist account on the internet. It has links to a movement leader
candidates.description: The account Rise of Alberta is anonymous and drives four times as much engagement as the next most popular account.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman in fake nurse case once again avoids sentencing after 6th postponement
candidates.description: Lisa Driscoll didn't show up to court on Thursday for what was supposed to be her long-awaited sentencing hearing. Lucky for her, the judge wasn't there either.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Michael J. Fox promoted within Order of Canada
candidates.description: Famed actor Michael J. Fox has been promoted to companion of the Order of Canada, the highest level within the order. The Order of Canada is meant to recognize people who make 'extraordinary contributions to the nation,' according to the Governor General of Canada website. Fox is also a vocal advocate in raising awareness for people living with Parkinson's disease. The actor went public with news he had Parkinson's in 1998 and is a co-founder of the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada scores a dairy win on U.S. soil as farmers grumble about Trump's trade war
candidates.description: At the World Dairy Expo in Wisconsin, the political tension between Canada and the U.S. is — more or less — set aside as farmers from both sides of the border focus on their best bovines. But even so, CBC News found some Americans in the crowd who take a dim view of the Trump administration's trade war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strikes kill 5, including 4 women, in Gaza, health officials say
candidates.description: An Israeli airstrike killed at least five Palestinians, including four women, in an apartment building in Gaza City early on Saturday, health and civil defence service officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: G7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel, amid energy crunch
candidates.description: The release would begin immediately and take four months, starting with a "substantial" diesel release within the first 20 days. Diesel prices have soared globally due to the oil supply crunch brought on by fighting in the Middle East between the U.S. and Iran.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CBS Sports describes Tony Romo's permanent exit as mutual parting
candidates.description: CBS Sports and Tony Romo have officially parted ways, one month after the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback pleaded no contest to charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'I was fighting for my life': Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls FlyDubai cockpit attack
candidates.description: The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Christa Pike on ventilator after surviving Tennessee execution attempt, lawyer says
candidates.description: Christa Pike, convicted of killing a classmate in 1995 when she was 18, is receiving breathing assistance from a ventilator after Tennessee's attempt to execute her by lethal injection failed earlier this week, her attorneys say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak surpasses 4,000 deaths amid violence and mistrust
candidates.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has recorded more than 4,000 deaths, authorities say, as they struggle to contain the spread of the virus.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cornell 7: Governor vows to change N.Y. rape law that makes reporting hard when intoxication present
candidates.description: New York's governor and attorney general were set to give an update Friday morning about the investigation into a woman's allegations that she was gang raped at a Cornell University fraternity house beginning at 9:30 a.m. ET.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard speaks out about death of her ex-fiancé, Ken Urker
candidates.description: Gypsy Rose Blanchard, who spent more than seven years in prison for her mother's murder, is speaking out after Ken Urker, her former fiancé and the father of her daughter, died yesterday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Prepared ourselves for the worst': FlyDubai passenger recounts moments during cockpit attack
candidates.description: Almog Italie and his family were on the final leg of their trip home following a vacation in Japan when they felt FlyDubai flight FZ1073 plummet. Italie was one of 174 people on board the plane earlier this week when one of the pilots stabbed the other in an attempt to crash the plane. The flight plunged 30,000 feet in under 30 seconds.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The Black Sea is the most dangerous it's been since the start of Russia’s war. And it's choking global grain
candidates.description: Strikes against ports and vessels have crippled shipping routes leaving Russia's and Ukraine's combined wheat exports down by 60 per cent over last year. Global wheat prices are already up from a year ago, and experts warn it could get worse.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In Gaza, a UN cash-for-work program gives Palestinians some income — and hope
candidates.description: The UN World Food Program's cash-for-work program helps provide stable work and income for Palestinians in Gaza, who have with little to no other options.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Macron government struggles to quell protests as riot police clash with high schoolers
candidates.description: Riot police clashed with high school students across France on Friday and unions called for teachers to strike as President Emmanuel Macron's government battled to contain increasingly ‌violent protests over classroom conditions and funding.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New York's governor removes district attorney from Cornell rape allegations case, appoints special prosecutor
candidates.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed a special prosecutor Thursday to oversee an investigation into a woman's allegations that she was gang raped at a Cornell University fraternity house, with the governor saying she had lost faith in the local district attorney's ability to handle the case.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa launches new national AI council to advise on safety, deployment
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney's new national council on artificial intelligence is meant to provide the government with guidance on the evolution of its AI strategy and on making the technology safer.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Undetected software issue knocked out 911 for several provinces last month, Bell report says
candidates.description: A 911 outage that lasted nearly an hour and a half in several Canadian provinces last month was caused by a previously undetected bug in Bell's software, the company said in a report on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney, Smith say new West Coast pipeline could get oil companies building again
candidates.description: It's been a relatively quiet decade in Alberta's oilsands, but the federal and provincial governments believe a new West Coast pipeline coupled with policy shifts might help turn up the volume. Prime Minister Mark Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith say that if oilsands companies start building again — as they hope — it will be different this time around.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
candidates.description: Pike's lawyers said the failure "goes far beyond any one person". Pike is in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
candidates.description: The man accused of trying to take over the Israel-bound jet is named as Hamam al-Hammami by several media outlets.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
candidates.description: The strike on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge comes after repeat attacks on another major bridge in Ukraine's capital.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
candidates.description: More than 50 protests are taking place on Saturday after the government failed to get emergency legislation through parliament.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: G7 to release millions of barrels of oil and diesel after Trump threat
candidates.description: The co-ordinated release is aimed at heading off further price spikes and avoiding a ban on US diesel exports.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why has Brazil accused the US of election interference?
candidates.description: The Latin American country will vote for its next president, as Lula da Silva and Bolsonaro clash over sovereignty, security and ties with Washington.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Kim wins Asian Games gold to secure military exemption
candidates.description: Golfer Tom Kim wins gold at the Asian Games to secure an exemption from mandatory service in South Korea's military.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Hawaii's iconic 550-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch collapses
candidates.description: The lava rock formation protruding from the rocky cliffs of Volcanoes National Park crumbled some time last weekend.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot
candidates.description: Capt Smit Machchhar tells Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi he opened the cockpit door to let others in during the attack.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination'
candidates.description: Israel's prime minister says the pilot who tried to take over the Flydubai plane clearly intended to "down the plane".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
candidates.description: The Russian leader insists Moscow is "not threatening anyone" and is merely responding to statements by Western leaders.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
candidates.description: For the first time in three decades there has not been a single Atlantic hurricane in September, normally the most active month.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Joker persona helps Cong 'feel the fear' in opponents
candidates.description: Wang Cong dismisses critics who say she she is not deserving of facing Natalia Silva for the flyweight world title at UFC 332 on Saturday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'
candidates.description: The discovery of 12 women's bodies near Johannesburg has again highlighted South Africa's problem with violence against women.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's
candidates.description: Texas reporter Michael Graczyk has seen botched executions in his time, but not one in which an inmate survived.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: School protests send shivers down French government's spine
candidates.description: A movement that started nearly two weeks ago has spread, and in France young people on the streets spells trouble, writes Hugh Schofield.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Will Spain's housing crisis lead to a snap election?
candidates.description: The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is in Madrid, where a series of marches have been scheduled, after Spain's Congress rejected measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Newly released video shows Luigi Mangione’s arrest
candidates.description: The bodycam footage also shows a police officer finding a gun in Mangione's backpack, days after the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How widely used is the death penalty in the US?
candidates.description: The death penalty is back in the news after Christa Pike survived two lethal injection attempts in Tennessee - but how widely used is it in the US?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What we know about Christa Pike’s condition after failed execution
candidates.description: The BBC’s Ione Wells reports from outside the Tennessee hospital where Pike is said to have arrived Wednesday night after surviving two lethal injection attempts.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: I'm a wildlife cameraman but 'special' rare sightings can still take me by surprise
candidates.description: Wildlife cameraman Dan Abbot is caught off guard by a humpback whale, a rare sight in Welsh waters.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
candidates.description: The world-famous Palm House at the Royal Botanic Gardens Kew in London is about to undergo a massive makeover.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected
candidates.description: The Lost Woods of the Low Weald and Downs project aims to restore some of Sussex's ancient woodland.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Brazil's big political rematch: What to know about the Brazilian election
candidates.description: Four years after President Lula narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil is back at the ballot box. This time, Lula faces Bolsonaro's son, Flávio, in a high-stakes rematch.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How Brazil's two leading presidential candidates are talking about crime
candidates.description: Crime is at the top of voters' concerns in Brazil ahead of Sunday's national elections. Many are calling for tougher measures — part of a broader rightward shift across Latin America.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The G7 will release 100 million reserve barrels of diesel fuel over the next 4 months
candidates.description: After increased pressure from Washington, the G7 held an emergency meeting on energy. The world's wealthiest nations say they will release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel in their reserves.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Germany's political center fights for relevance after far-right and far-left gains
candidates.description: Centrist politicians are soul-searching after electoral gains by the far right and the far left. Today's weak coalitions, political fragmentation and dire economy echo a past that led to the rise of fascism.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: October 1 ushered in a new era in U.S. foreign aid. What's the plan? Will it work?
candidates.description: The America First strategy asks for a Memorandum of Understanding as a condition for healthcare and development aid. It's been praised for promoting self-reliance but criticized for its conditions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Cloaked in anonymity, Israeli soldiers describe mass civilian killings in 'NAZA'
candidates.description: NAZA is an acronym for nezek agavi , Hebrew for "collateral damage." It refers to the number of civilian casualties the Israeli military deems acceptable. The documentary is made by Israeli filmmakers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Cornell rape case gets special prosecutor. And, Renee Good's family sues the government
candidates.description: New legal action in two closely watched cases: one at Cornell, the other over Renee Good's death. We take a closer look.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pro-democracy activists increasingly vulnerable to authoritarian governments in Southeast Asia
candidates.description: Activists across Asia are being hunted down by authoritarian governments even across international borders. Human rights groups have been warning of a "swap market" of repression in Southeast Asia.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Economist Betsey Stevenson breaks down the gender gap in recent hiring reports
candidates.description: The U.S. economy added fewer jobs than expected last month and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Betsey Stevenson, an economist at the University of Michigan.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pro-Trump Influencer Benny Johnson is being sued for defamation by ICE protesters
candidates.description: The lawsuit says the prominent conservative podcaster falsely claimed the protesters were assaulting ICE officers during demonstrations at an ICE facility in Illinois last year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September as job market lacks spark
candidates.description: U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September as the unemployment rate inched up to 4.2%. Job gains for July and August were revised down by a total of 60,000 jobs, extending a lackluster run for the job market.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why is diesel more expensive than regular gas?
candidates.description: Diesel hasn't always been more expensive than other gasoline. Then in 2004, a switch happened due to air quality standards, demand, and taxes. In this week's Indicator newsletter, we dig into diesel prices, what kind of fun people are buying, and other forms of making your tax bill smaller.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
candidates.description: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. Senate is up for grabs. Can this Ohio Democrat win back working class votes?
candidates.description: After 32 years in Congress, Ohio's Sherrod Brown lost his Senate seat in 2024 as many working class voters turned out for Trump. Now Brown is counting on union voters to send him back to Washington.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Breweries adapt as tastes in beer change
candidates.description: The craft beer market is saturated and tastes are changing. Brewers are coming with innovative ways to attract customers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 4 ways to battle performance anxiety, according to a confidence coach
candidates.description: Worried about stumbling before a high-stakes event, like a race or a job interview? Psychologist Cindra Kamphoff offers creative strategies to overcome the jitters and build confidence in the moment.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Heat-related deaths in Phoenix rise, after two years of decline
candidates.description: Metro Phoenix has so far seen twice as many heat deaths as this time last year. Authorities are trying to understand why and how to intervene.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'It's a nightmare.' Former refugee, professor on Trump's new Medicaid policy
candidates.description: Starting Oct. 1, many immigrants who are here legally lose their Medicaid coverage because of the Republican budget bill passed last year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new California law bans child marriage. What's the global outlook on the practice?
candidates.description: The governor of California has signed into law a ban on child marriage. What is the status of other efforts to ban the practice? And do bans prove effective?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: The United States Geological Survey reported an earthquake of magnitude 4.7. The event occurred near 5 km NNE of Korumburra, Australia. Official monitoring data may be updated as scientists review additional measurements.
candidates.author: U.S. Geological Survey
